name: Vicente Huidobro
credit: Photograph of Vicente Huidobro, unknown photographer, early 20th century · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Vicente Huidobro (Santiago, 1893 - Cartagena, Chile, 1948) was a Chilean poet who lived much of his life in Paris and Madrid. He was the founder and chief theorist of Creacionismo, which held that a poem should make a new reality in words, not describe the one outside it, and he worked beside Apollinaire, Reverdy and the Cubist painters.

His best-known book is Altazor o el viaje en paracaídas, begun in 1919 and first published complete in Madrid in 1931. It follows a falling aviator-poet through seven cantos, from a prose preface to a last canto of pure invented sound. Huidobro also wrote Horizon carré, Ecuatorial and Temblor de cielo, and died in 1948.
